summary.text: Elias Montgomery, an unaffiliated recent University of Utah graduate who works as a policy analyst, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Utah's open 1st Congressional District to Ben McAdams.

He described himself as an independent alternative to the two major parties, focused on housing costs and what he called a "broken political system." His platform included limits on institutional purchases of single-family homes, "missing-middle" housing, and a proportional nomination model for parties.

paragraphs.text: Montgomery graduated from West Jordan High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Utah in 2025. He works as a policy analyst.

He ran without a party affiliation. In his Ballotpedia survey he listed his key messages as housing affordability, restoring voter power through a proportional nomination model and ending corporate subsidies, and local control, including opposition to the Box Elder data center proposal.
He received 1.4% of the vote to Ben McAdams's 70.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
